entries.issue: Does intensive medical therapy improve outcomes in patients with MVD compared with standard secondary prevention?
entries.suggested_research: Trials comparing intensive secondary prevention vs usual care to evaluate whether the former strategy improves clinical outcomes.

entries.issue: The clinical utility of hybrid coronary revascularization in ACS patients with multivessel CAD is uncertain.
entries.suggested_research: Randomized controlled trials assessing the clinical benefit of hybrid revascularization.

entries.issue: How to better differentiate Type 2 from Type 1 MI before invasive assessment.
entries.suggested_research: Prospective evaluation of diagnostic strategies aimed at better classifying patients according to their type of MI (Type 1 vs. Type 2).

entries.issue: The optimal management strategy in older adults with NSTE-ACS is not known.
entries.suggested_research: Further studies recruiting older adults to evaluate whether the current standard of care also benefits this subset of patients.

entries.issue: The optimal management strategy in older frail, comorbid adults with NSTE-ACS is not known.
entries.suggested_research: Older frail, comorbid patients should not be systematically excluded from RCTs; prospective studies targeting this group are needed.

entries.issue: The optimal management strategy in older frail, comorbid adults with STEMI is not known.
entries.suggested_research: Prospective data are needed to better understand optimal management strategies in this subgroup.

entries.issue: Optimal antiplatelet therapy and its duration to manage ACS in pregnant patients are not known.
entries.suggested_research: Prospective data are needed to determine which antiplatelet therapy regimen and duration is best for pregnant women with ACS.

entries.issue: The optimal management strategy for pregnant women with NSTE-ACS is not known.
entries.suggested_research: Observational data in pregnant patients with ACS are needed to evaluate risks and outcomes; targeted studies to define management strategies in pregnancy are required.

entries.issue: There is a need to further evaluate the contribution of social determinants of health.
entries.suggested_research: Observational data to assess the impact of social determinants on clinical outcomes in ACS and randomized interventions aimed at reducing social inequalities to evaluate how to reduce outcome gaps.

content.notes: Content extracted from a guideline table listing unresolved clinical questions (left column) and recommended research or actions (right column). Acronyms: MVD (multivessel disease), ACS (acute coronary syndrome), CAD (coronary artery disease), NSTE-ACS (non–ST-elevation ACS), STEMI (ST-elevation myocardial infarction).
